name: Pint of View Lecture: Why Good Journalism is Behind a Paywall—Who Pays for It & What Does It Cost?
description:
Welcome to Pint of View – Bangalore's first-ever community where classroom-styled lectures meet drinks in pubs and bars.

About the lecture

The question of who pays for journalism is ultimately a question about what kind of journalism we get.

Indian journalism operates under competing pressures. Television news is driven by TRPs and the race for attention. Digital newsrooms contend with clicks and algorithms. Advertising remains a major source of revenue, but can also shape what gets covered.

When revenue follows clicks, journalism competes with everything else that can generate them. Complex stories that take weeks to report rarely perform as well as outrage produced in minutes. This raises a basic question: what does independence mean? Can a newsroom remain independent when its survival depends on advertising or audience numbers?

There is an older model worth revisiting. Indian newspapers and magazines once relied more directly on circulation and subscriptions, with readers as paying customers. During the freedom movement, publications were spaces for public debate. Gandhi and Ambedkar understood journalism as a way to challenge power and give communities a voice.

The paywall is one answer to journalism’s economic problem. Asking readers to pay can give journalists room to pursue expensive reporting. But if good journalism sits behind a subscription, what happens to those who cannot afford it?

This lecture examines the changing economics of Indian media and asks what independent journalism can look like today.

If nobody pays for independent journalism, who eventually does?

About the speaker

In a news landscape crowded with instant reactions and louder voices, Pooja Prasanna’s journalism is driven by a different question: what lies beneath the headline? For more than 17 years, she has reported on politics, governance, elections, social justice and public policy across south India, with a particular interest in how power shapes public life.

Pooja is currently the Editorial Head for Reporting at The News Minute, where she leads political coverage, ground reporting, investigations and public-interest journalism. She anchors

Let Me Explain, a weekly explainer series that makes complex political, legal and policy questions accessible, and co-hosts South Central, TNM’s flagship podcast on politics and public affairs.

Her reporting focuses on the institutions and systems that shape democracy in practice. She has covered elections, electoral rolls, political financing, communal mobilisation and changing political landscapes, often examining their consequences beyond the immediate news cycle.

Before joining The News Minute, Pooja was a Principal Correspondent at Times Now and later South India Bureau Chief at Republic TV, reporting on politics and breaking news across the region. Her television experience strengthened her ground-up, fact-based approach to reporting in fast-moving and highly charged environments.

In February 2025, she delivered a TEDx talk in Bengaluru, Claiming the Narrative: Truth, Power, and the Fight for Autonomy, exploring storytelling, identity, power and resilience in an era of contested truths.

Event Details

  • The Humming Tree, Indiranagar

  • Tuesday, 25 August | 7 PM to 9 PM [Gates open at 6 pm, please try to arrive early, so we complete your check-in in time]

Note: There’s a mandatory cover charge of ₹500 to be paid at the venue upon arriving, redeemable against any F&B.

Seating will be on first-come, first-served basis.

What to Expect:

  • A 60-minute lecture

  • 30–45 minutes of interactive Q&A

  • Social mixer and personal Q&As with the lecturer

About Pint of View

Inspired by the successful Lectures on Tap community in the U.S., Pint of View brings this format to India for the first time. It’s where big ideas meet bar tables, and where you enjoy a drink in hand, walking out with a new way of seeing the world.

Book now & develop your own pint of view! 🍻

name: Dough it Yourself: A Turkish Pide Making Experience
description:
Step into the Kitchen Studio for a hands-on session built around one of Turkey’s most loved flatbreads.

Soft dough is stretched, shaped, and filled, each pide coming together with its own character. Think spinach with goat cheese, roasted vegetables layered over a smoked tomato base.

There’s a rhythm to it, shaping, filling, baking, watching the edges turn golden and crisp while the centre stays soft.

Take it slow, build it the way it feels right, and finish with something warm, fresh from the oven.

Sit down with it while it’s still hot, or take it home to share.

Head to our Kitchen Studio on the first floor once you arrive at the venue.

name: Manual 3.0
description:
MANUAL 3.0

What does it look like when a craft refuses to disappear?

Manual is our ongoing analog culture revival at The Commons - a space to slow down, rediscover fading crafts, and put them back into people’s hands.

Manual 3.0 is about enamel painting. Meet Surabhi, an artist from Kannur who has spent years hand-painting the bold, brush-lettered signage that once covered shopfronts, walls and banners - before flex boards took over. Think Nirma ads, toothpaste walls and playful beedi art. No stencils. No digital tools. Just muscle memory and a steady hand.

Come experience an enamel painting workshop and explore his living gallery at The Commons.

“Some crafts don't need saving. They just need a room to keep living in.”

What's the lineup?
12:00pm – Doors open with vinyl, food & drinks
12:30pm – Meet the artist
1:00pm – Explore the gallery
1:30–3:30pm – Hands-on enamel painting workshop

Come with curiosity. We’ll take care of the rest.

Ajji House by Subko, Bangalore | August 30th | 12pm onwards

Can’t make the workshop? The gallery stays live until September 5th.

name: Side A/Side B: The Music of Blood, Sweat & Tears with Bruce Lee Mani
description:
“They didn’t invent Jazz-Rock, but they sure played the hell out of it.”

For this edition of Side A / Side B, musician, songwriter and Thermal and A Quarter frontman Bruce Lee Mani takes us through the music of Blood, Sweat & Tears, a band whose sound has stayed with him through his own life in music.

Their music was unlike anything he had heard before. The voice of David Clayton-Thomas, the writing, the collision of jazz and rock. For a 17-year-old in Bangalore with big musical dreams, it opened up a whole new world of what music could sound like.

Through a personal selection from their extraordinary body of work, Bruce traces the music that shaped him, the sounds that stuck and the influence they would have on the musician he went on to become.

A listening session about influence, discovery and the records that stay with you.

Please Note: Rs 1000 cover included with your ticket.

name: munnuDi kannaDa - Weekend Basic Spoken Kannada Classes with Pradeep Khaadri
description:
A 12-session beginner-friendly Kannada course designed to help you navigate everyday life in Bengaluru. Through interactive classes held every Monday and Tuesday over six weeks, you’ll build useful vocabulary, essential grammar, and conversational skills to understand and speak basic Kannada with confidence.

Schedule (12 classes)

Every Saturday and Sunday for six weeks from 12th September to 25th October - 10am to 12pm (No session on 17th and 18th October)

Week 1

Saturday, 12th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 13th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Week 2

Saturday, 19th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 20th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Week 3

Saturday, 26th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 27th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Week 4

Saturday, 3rd Oct - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 4th Oct - 10am - 12pm

Week 5

Saturday, 10th Oct - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 11Oct - 10am - 12pm

BREAK

No session on October 17th and 18th

Week 6

Saturday, 24th Oct - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 25th Oct - 10am - 12pm

Course objectives

- To understand the spoken language

- To construct simple sentences

- To make simple conversation as required in day to day activities

Broad areas covered in the module

- Vocabulary building

- Basic sentence structure

- Use of subjects in first, second and third person and cases

- Common verbs and their conjugation in different tenses

- Hands on exercises in sentence construction and conversation

Key features

- Elaborate explanation in Hindi, English, Tamil and Telugu (as required)

- Easy learning using grammar rules

- Personalised attention to each learner

- Separate WhatsApp group for continued learning

- Limited batch size for focused training

Who is Pradeep Khaadri and come-nuDi?

Mr. Pradeep Khaadri hails from a family of teachers and has proficiency in five languages, and an insatiable thirst for learning more. He has successfully trained several batches of learners of different age groups, linguistic, cultural, educational, and professional backgrounds over the past eight years.
